messages:
marta (AE): AurumPay asked for a compact perf validation: steady 120 qps chat (512 seq), 5m microbursts up to 700 qps, and a cost/latency comparison between redwood-7b-4bit and redwood-7b-fp32. They also want reproducible CI steps and a short security note on prompt retention.

diego (SRE): Proposed run: 10m warm, 35m steady @120 qps, bursts: 2m@300, 2m@500, 5m@700, cooldown 8m. Collect p50/p95/p99/p99.9, GPU slice util, batch hist, and cache hit ratio. tag runs with: customer=aurumpay env=bench.

rav (SE): If their p95 SLO is 200ms, we should flag that 4bit meets steady but might need Dedicated or faster autoscale for repeated 700 qps bursts. We should include a routing fallback plan.

eli (Solutions Eng): Cost estimate quick take: assume avg output 80 toks/resp. Token math: 120 qps * 80 = 9.6k tok/s => 829M tok/day if sustained. Using list-rate token prices (example): fp32 ~ $0.0000010/token, 4bit ~ $0.00000038/token. I'll compute exact numbers in sheet.

ci-bot: CI job aurumpay-bench-v1 queued (id: ci-aurum-2024-07-01)

diego (SRE): Bench profile (summary):
```
models: [redwood-7b-4bit, redwood-7b-fp32]
seq_prompt: 128
seq_resp_avg: 384
qps_steps: [steady:120, spikes:300,500,700]
batch_targets: {4bit:8, fp32:16}
warmup: populate kv cache with 6k sample prompts
metrics: latency_histogram_ms, gpu_util_pct, batch_size_dist, dropped_requests_count
```

marta (AE): Please add the exact run command we can paste into CI. AurumPay's auditors will want the command that produced the artifacts.

diego (SRE): Pasteable example:
```bash
./tools/bench_runner \
  --profile profiles/aurumpay_burst.json \
  --model redwood-7b-4bit \
  --duration 3600 \
  --output gs://redwood-temp/aurumpay/run-4bit.json \
  --meta "customer=aurumpay,run=multi-sla" \
  --redact-prompts true
```
Redact flag will hash inputs; we store only hashes + token counts for compliance.

rav (SE): Also add note: if they require HSM-backed KMS proofs, Dedicated or Private deployment is recommended. Hosted runs store artifacts in encrypted buckets for a limited window.

eli (Solutions Eng): Ops note: enable routing fallback in the test: when avg latency > 500ms for >10s, route new requests to 4bit variant for burst traffic. We'll show how that affects p99.9 in the writeup.

marta (AE): Who owns the writeup + cost appendix? Need 1-pager + 3-slide deck for the customer meeting Tuesday.

rav (SE): I can own the writeup. Template: TL;DR, test setup, per-model heatmap, p95/p99/p99.9 table, GPU util and batch histogram, cost appendix, recommendation.

eli (Solutions Eng): I'll produce the cost sheet and a short note on enterprise commit discounts.

ci-bot: CI job aurumpay-bench-v1 started on runner-us-east-1

diego (SRE): interim update: steady 120 qps on 4bit for 35m complete. Results: p50 40ms, p95 140ms, p99 300ms, p99.9 580ms. gpu_util ~58%, batch median 8, no drops. Uploading: gs://redwood-temp/aurumpay/interim-4bit.json

marta (AE): Nice. Share quick chart screenshots in thread if possible.

diego (SRE): queued fp32 run.

ci-bot: aurumpay-bench-v1 runner reported: quota bump applied for temporary burst capacity

diego (SRE): final: both runs complete. Final aggregated numbers (topline):
- redwood-7b-4bit: steady p95 150ms, burst@700 p95 520ms, burst@700 p99.9 1.05s
- redwood-7b-fp32: steady p95 95ms, burst@700 p95 240ms, burst@700 p99.9 720ms
Cost delta observed: fp32 ~3.2x per-token cost vs 4bit in this run.

rav (SE): Interpretation: 4bit is cost-efficient for steady and moderate bursts, but for tight tail under heavy bursts fp32 on Dedicated is safer. We'll show suggested autoscale targets (slice counts) to reduce tail at 700 qps on hosted.

eli (Solutions Eng): Cost appendix: attached spreadsheet link: https://sheets.redwood/aurumpay/costs (will attach in deck). Note: this run assumed no encryption-overhead pricing and no sustained commit discounts.

marta (AE): Security note for auditors: run used --redact-prompts, we can provide hash manifest and deletion logs. Also artifacts stored in encrypted bucket for 30 days and shared via signed URL for 7 days.

diego (SRE): uploaded full artifacts and profiles: gs://redwood-temp/aurumpay/final/ (permissions set)

rav (SE): I'll draft the 1-pager and drop link. ETA 18:00 PST tomorrow.

eli (Solutions Eng): I'll add pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated monthly commit) to the appendix.

marta (AE): Great work. Action items: diego upload run profiles + redact proof, rav write the results doc, eli finish cost appendix, marta prep deck. Meeting Tuesday noon PT. :rocket:
